title: Create Sorted Array through Instructions
statement:
Begin with an empty container `nums`, then take the values of the integer array `instructions` one by one from left to right and put each into `nums` so that `nums` stays sorted. Putting a value `x` in costs the smaller of two counts taken just before it goes in:

- how many elements already in `nums` are strictly less than `x`;
- how many elements already in `nums` are strictly greater than `x`.

Elements equal to `x` count toward neither side. Return the total cost of inserting every value of `instructions`. The total can be large, so return it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

The cost of each insertion only needs two counts over the values inserted so far: how many are below `x` and how many are above it. Recounting by scanning `nums` (or keeping a real sorted array and splicing) is O(n²), too slow for 10^5 values. A Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree) indexed by value keeps "how many inserted values are at most `v`" for every `v`, and both answers and updates take O(log M), where M is the largest value.

## Approach

1. Make `tree` with one slot per value from 1 to `maxValue`.
2. `add(value)` records one more copy of `value`; `countUpTo(value)` returns how many inserted values are `<= value`.
3. For the value at position `inserted` (so `inserted` values are already in):
   - `smaller = countUpTo(value - 1)`, the values strictly below it;
   - `larger = inserted - countUpTo(value)`, the values strictly above it.
4. Add `min(smaller, larger)` to `cost` modulo `10^9 + 7`, then `add(value)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`instructions = [1, 5, 6, 2]`, `maxValue = 6`.

| inserted | value | smaller | larger | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 − 0 = 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 5 | 1 | 1 − 1 = 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 6 | 2 | 2 − 2 = 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 1 | 3 − 1 = 2 | 1 |

The total cost is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log M): each value does two prefix queries and one update.
- Space: O(M) for the tree, M = the largest value (at most 10^5).

## Pitfalls

- Equal values are neither smaller nor larger: use `countUpTo(value - 1)` for `smaller` but `countUpTo(value)` for `larger`.
- Query before you add the current value, or it counts itself.
- Fenwick indexes start at 1; the loops step with `i & -i` and stop at 0.
- At the full limits the total reaches about 2.5 · 10^9, so take it modulo `10^9 + 7`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tree` | the Fenwick tree of counts, indexed by value |
| `maxValue` | the largest value, the size of the tree |
| `inserted` | how many values are already in `nums` |
| `smaller`, `larger` | inserted values strictly below / above `value` |
| `cost` | total cost so far, modulo `10^9 + 7` |
